# Authentication, Credentials and Sessions (AUTH)

## SCS-AUTH-01 Use standard identity protocols and the organization's identity provider

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Applications MUST authenticate users with OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect or token-based mechanisms (JWT) issued by an approved identity provider, integrated with the organization's directory (Microsoft Entra ID / Active Directory) where possible. Custom authentication schemes MUST NOT be built. Identifiers such as employee number, phone or email alone MUST NOT be accepted as proof of identity.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Use ASP.NET Core Identity or JWT Bearer authentication (Microsoft.Identity.Web for Entra ID) on all API endpoints.
- Prefer an identity provider with asymmetric signing keys over minting tokens from a password POST.
- Authorization Code + PKCE (S256) for browser and native clients. Do not use the implicit flow or the resource owner password grant.

Verification: Architecture review confirms the identity provider and flow. No custom login/token code outside approved libraries.

## SCS-AUTH-02 Apply modern password rules and store passwords with an approved hash

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: Where an application manages its own passwords, it MUST follow NIST SP 800-63B-4: at least 15 characters when the password is the only factor (at least 8 when used with MFA), allow at least 64 characters, no composition rules, no forced periodic change, and a check against a list of breached or common passwords. Passwords MUST be stored only as salted hashes from an approved, slow password hashing function, and MUST NEVER be stored in plain text or with reversible encryption.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- ASP.NET Core Identity: set Password.RequiredLength = 15 (or 8 when MFA is enforced), turn off RequireDigit/RequireUppercase/RequireNonAlphanumeric, and add a breached-password validator (for example a k-anonymity Have I Been Pwned check).
- The Identity hasher (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512) defaults to 100,000 iterations; raise it: Configure<PasswordHasherOptions>(o => o.IterationCount = 220_000).
- Outside Identity, use Argon2id (m = 19 MiB, t = 2, p = 1) or PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with at least 600,000 iterations via Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2.
- Never use MD5, SHA-1 or a plain SHA-256 for passwords.
- Force a password change only when there is evidence of compromise.

Verification: Code review of Identity options and hasher configuration. Database check that no password column holds plain text.

## SCS-AUTH-03 Validate tokens fully on every request

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: Every API request carrying a token MUST have the token validated for signature, allowed algorithm, issuer, audience and expiry before any processing. Tokens MUST NOT be trusted after only being decoded.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- AddJwtBearer with TokenValidationParameters: ValidateIssuer, ValidateAudience, ValidateLifetime and ValidateIssuerSigningKey all true (ValidateIssuerSigningKey defaults to false).
- Set ValidAlgorithms to the expected algorithm only, and ClockSkew to 30 seconds (the default is 5 minutes).
- HS256 keys must be at least 256 random bits from Key Vault. Prefer RS256/ES256 tokens from the identity provider.
- Never authorize based on JwtSecurityTokenHandler.ReadJwtToken (it does not validate). Do not set RequireSignedTokens = false, RequireHttpsMetadata = false or a custom SignatureValidator.
- Set MapInboundClaims = false so the sub and role claim names stay as issued.

Verification: Negative tests with expired, wrong-audience, wrong-issuer, unsigned (alg none) and tampered tokens all return 401.

## SCS-AUTH-04 Limit failed login attempts and log them

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Failed authentication attempts MUST be logged and monitored. Login, one-time code, password reset and token refresh endpoints MUST be protected by account lockout or throttling (no more than 100 consecutive failures per account, and much lower for lockout), and MUST give the same response whether the user exists or not.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- ASP.NET Core Identity: call PasswordSignInAsync(..., lockoutOnFailure: true) (the template passes false). Defaults: MaxFailedAccessAttempts 5, lockout 5 minutes.
- Add a rate-limit policy on login, OTP, reset and refresh endpoints, partitioned by account and by client (see SCS-API-03).
- Log each failure with user identifier, source IP and time (never the password); alert on bursts (see SCS-LOG-03).
- Return the same message and similar timing for "no such user" and "wrong password".

Verification: Test: repeated failed logins trigger lockout or 429, and each attempt appears in the security log.

Current gap: IT-56 ASR-04 records this as partially implemented: logging in place and lockout applied on backend APIs; monitoring and alerting to be completed.

## SCS-AUTH-05 Require MFA for administrative, privileged and remote access

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Multi-factor authentication MUST be enforced for all administrative and privileged functions and for remote access, and SHOULD be offered wherever feasible for other users. At least one phishing-resistant option (for example passkeys or Microsoft Authenticator with number matching) SHOULD be available.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Use the identity provider's MFA (Entra ID Conditional Access) rather than building MFA in the application.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Admin portals and admin APIs require an "mfa" / "amr" claim from the identity provider in an authorization policy.
- ASP.NET Core Identity apps: enable TOTP authenticator support and require it for admin roles.

Verification: Test that admin endpoints reject tokens without MFA claims.

Current gap: IT-56 ASR-06 records MFA for admin portals as planned, depending on infrastructure support. IT-29 §9.4 already requires it, so this is a known gap that needs a remediation date.

## SCS-AUTH-06 Never ship or keep default credentials or test accounts

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Default credentials MUST NEVER be used in any environment. Test accounts, seed users and backdoor logins MUST NOT exist in production.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Change or disable vendor default accounts (SQL Server sa, SAP default users, admin/admin on appliances) before first use.
- Seed data scripts that create users run only in Development, guarded by an environment check.
- The pre-deployment checklist confirms no test accounts or hardcoded logins exist (see SCS-DEP-03).

Verification: Pre-deployment checklist item; periodic review of production user lists.

## SCS-AUTH-07 Manage sessions and tokens securely

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Sessions and tokens MUST have defined lifetimes, be stored securely (never in plain text on the device), be invalidated on logout and on password or role change, and be protected against hijacking and fixation. The server MUST enforce idle and absolute session timeouts.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Access tokens live 5 to 15 minutes. Refresh tokens are random, stored server-side only as a hash, bound to one user and device, rotated on every use (revoke the whole family if an old one is replayed), and have an absolute lifetime.
- Timeouts follow NIST SP 800-63B-4 AAL2: reauthenticate at least every 24 hours, and after at most 1 hour of inactivity (15 minutes for high-risk applications).

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Issue a new session identifier after login (cookie auth does this by default); never accept a session ID from the URL.
- Cookie auth: use an ITicketStore (SessionStore) so logout invalidates the session on the server; HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies (SCS-WEB-03).
- Call UserManager.UpdateSecurityStampAsync on password or role change so existing sessions are invalidated.
- Refresh tokens travel in the request body, never in a URL.

Verification: Tests: token expiry enforced; logout makes the old refresh token and cookie unusable; refresh token reuse revokes the session.
